name: Acute Biphenotypic Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO 2016 Classification for Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia

criteria.description: Leukemic blasts expressing markers of more than one hematopoietic lineage (myeloid and lymphoid) confirmed by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry
Presence of ≥20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Cytogenetic or molecular abnormalities supporting biphenotypic lineage involvement (e.g., t(9;22)(q34;q11), BCR-ABL1 fusion)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least 20% blasts in bone marrow or blood with immunophenotypic evidence of expression of markers from two distinct hematopoietic lineages
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other acute leukemias and confirmation by multiparameter flow cytometry.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Leukemic blast proliferation with biphenotypic immunophenotype
pathognomonic.notes: Defining pathological feature rather than clinical symptom

searchTerms: low blood counts from marrow crowding
reduced red, white cells and platelets

common.symptomName: Anemia-related pallor and dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: pale skin and shortness of breath
small skin spots from low platelets

common.symptomName: Fever due to infection or leukemic process

occasional.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement causing headache or cranial neuropathies

searchTerms: losing weight and sweating at night
difficulty breathing from blood cell buildup
shortness of breath from thick blood

occasional.symptomName: Hepatic dysfunction with elevated liver enzymes

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to leukemic infiltration

searchTerms: heart inflammation with fluid around heart

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing blasts with mixed lineage markers
Bone marrow biopsy with ≥20% blasts expressing myeloid and lymphoid markers
imaging: Chest X-ray may show mediastinal lymphadenopathy
genetic: Presence of BCR-ABL1 fusion gene in some cases
other: Flow cytometry demonstrating co-expression of myeloid and lymphoid antigens on blasts

distinguishingFeatures: Blasts express predominantly lymphoid markers without myeloid antigen co-expression
Different cytogenetic abnormalities typical for ALL
Presence of BCR-ABL1 fusion gene with blast transformation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive pancytopenia with bleeding and infections
High blast count with leukostasis causing respiratory or neurological compromise
references: Arber DA et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Béné MC et al. Mixed-phenotype acute leukemia: clinical and laboratory features and outcome in 100 patients. Blood. 2011.
